arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Andrew Frey argued for the side that brought the case, Wachovia Bank.
He stated the main office location defines the bank's state citizenship.
He rejected the idea that every branch office creates a new state of citizenship.
Chief Justice Roberts questioned whether the main office address changes with charter amendments.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests how federal courts determine a national bank's state citizenship. This status controls whether a federal court has jurisdiction over the bank.

paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on November 28, 2005.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Wachovia Bank wants the Court to limit state citizenship to the main office location.
Schmidt wants the Court to count every branch office location as a state of citizenship.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Wachovia Bank argues the main office defines the bank's state citizenship under federal law.
Schmidt argues the bank is a citizen of every state where it maintains a branch.
